policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'he sent by his disciples' renders the preposition dia with the disciples as agents; RP's duo would give 'two of his disciples', a numeral the ASV does not have.

The ASV reproduces the base clause-linking exactly, including its asymmetry: 'and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, and the dead are raised up, and the poor have good tidings' — a connective at every join but the one the Greek also leaves unjoined. RP's omission would drop one of the 'and's the ASV prints.
ean and an in 'whosoever shall find no occasion of stumbling' are the same generalising particle spelled two ways; 'whosoever' renders either identically and no ASV note touches it.

'clothed in soft raiment' reads the same whether himatiois stands with malakois or the noun is left to be understood, and the ASV's second clause supplies 'raiment' for a Greek phrase that has no noun; no note is mapped here.
ASV 'kings' houses' renders a genitive plural of 'king' (basileon) as possessor; RP's basileion would give palaces/royal houses rather than houses belonging to kings.
English requires the copula in 'they that wear soft raiment are in kings' houses' whether eisin stands in the Greek or is understood, so the ASV cannot distinguish presence from omission.

ASV text 'But wherefore went ye out? to see a prophet?' breaks the question after the verb and puts 'to see' with 'a prophet', which is the base order and punctuation; the mapped textual_variant note gives the other arrangement, 'But what went ye out to see? a prophet?', as what many ancient authorities read — i.e. as the reading not adopted.
ASV 'This is he, of whom it is written' has no 'for'; the ASV renders gar elsewhere in this chapter, so the added conjunction is absent from the text translated.

ASV text reads 'He that hath ears to hear', with the infinitive; the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities omit to hear' marks the base's shorter reading as the one relegated to the margin.

ASV 'children sitting in the marketplaces, who call unto their fellows' subordinates the calling as a relative clause, matching the base's relative plus participle; RP coordinates with kai prosphonousin, which the ASV would render 'and call'. The ASV also keeps the article, 'the marketplaces'.
'and say' follows a preceding relative clause where English needs a connective regardless, so the 'and' does not show whether kai stood before legousin.
The ASV prints 'We piped unto you' but plain 'we wailed', keeping the dative in the first member and not the second; RP's added humin would give 'we wailed unto you' to match.
ASV text 'wisdom is justified by her works' renders ergon; the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read children' assigns RP's teknon to the margin.
ASV 'Then began he to upbraid' carries only the pronoun; the added subject ho Iesous would appear as 'Jesus', which the ASV does not print here.

ASV 'shalt thou be exalted unto heaven?' is the base's question with me and the future indicative; RP's participial he ... hupsotheisa is a relative description ('which art exalted unto heaven'), not a question.

ASV text 'thou shalt go down unto Hades' is the active katabese; the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read be brought down' puts RP's causative passive katabibasthese in the margin.
egenethesan and egenonto are alternative aorist forms of the same verb; 'had been done' and 'were done' render either, and the verse's notes address other points.
ASV 'it would have remained until this day' has a singular verb with Sodom as subject, matching the singular emeinen; RP's plural emeinan would require a plural subject and rendering.
'thou didst hide these things' renders ekrupsas and the compound apekrupsas alike; the only note on the verse is an alternative_rendering for 'I thank thee'.
The two readings differ only in the order of eudokia and egeneto; 'for so it was well-pleasing in thy sight' follows English order either way.
